findings.claim: The change removes the `case <= byte.MaxValue` UInt8 branch from the unsigned integer writer. This is unrelated to REQ-2283, and it changes the wire encoding. Values 128..255 now fall through to UInt16 (0xCD + 2 bytes) instead of UInt8 (0xCC + 1 byte), which gives non-canonical, larger output and breaks byte-compat expectations. The ledger flags numeric serialization as bug-prone [L13].

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize uint/ulong/int values 128..255 (e.g. 200) with base-built and head-built MessagePack; compare bytes. Base gives CC C8, head gives CD 00 C8. Existing writer tests asserting UInt8 should also fail.

findings.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in the compilation's own syntax trees. This includes Location.None diagnostics, such as the MemberNeedsKey diagnostic when FirstOrDefault returns null. This matches the deliberate design that referenced-assembly types are not analysed and the defining assembly owns validation [L12]. The README and MsgPack004 docs say the same, so the silent drop is expected.

receipt_plan.detail: [L12] Types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed; a missing diagnostic for them is not a defect.
